subject: Request: consolidated per-route economics view + exception runbook
messages:
From: Emma Walsh <emma@nimbushealth.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, ops@nimbushealth.com
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: consolidated per-route economics view + exception runbook

Hi Dylan,

Quick ask from our platform team: we need a consolidated per-route view that shows cost per 1k tokens, p50/p95 latency, and recent tail events for the last 30 days. The goal is two-fold: 1) help product owners identify expensive routes, and 2) onboard a simple exception runbook that engineers can follow when a route shows sudden cost or latency regression.

Attached is a small sample export from our side (nimbus-route-sample.csv) that shows the kinds of route names and IDs we use. Can Redwood provide a recommended console dashboard layout and an initial runbook template? We need something we can share with our SREs by next week.

Also copied ops for any immediate constraints on the telemetry side.

Thanks,
Emma Walsh
Director, Platform Engineering
Nimbus Health

Attachments: nimbus-route-sample.csv (csv, 28 KB)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Walsh <emma@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated per-route economics view + exception runbook

On Thu, 12 Aug 2027 at 09:14 AM Emma Walsh <emma@nimbushealth.com> wrote:
> Quick ask from our platform team: we need a consolidated per-route view that shows cost per 1k tokens, p50/p95 latency, and recent tail events for the last 30 days.

Thanks for the clear ask, Emma. Ava/Grace/Markus - can we treat this as a lightweight product request with two deliverables: a console dashboard wireframe (per-route cards + table) and an exception runbook draft that maps alerts to triage steps and fallback policies?

Initial thoughts:
- Dashboard: per-route card includes route name/ID, 30d cost, cost delta vs prior period, p50/p95 latency, error rate, and a small sparkline for traffic. Include a top-5 callers breakdown for chargeback.
- Alerts: set a composite alert for
  * cost spike: 30% delta in 24h or cost > budget threshold
  * latency tail: p95 > SLO or p99 jump by 2x
- Runbook: map each alert to who owns triage, immediate mitigation (traffic reroute, rate limit, model variant fallback), and follow-up items (postmortem, quota change).

I started a draft runbook file and added a sample structure. Attaching exception-runbook-draft.md. Can Markus scope the telemetry work (what we need from instrumentation and labels) and Ava/Grace take the dashboard wireframe?

Timeline: prototype wireframe by Tuesday, initial runbook by Wednesday; we can sync with Emma on Thursday if that works.

Thanks,
Dylan
Sr. Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference

Attachments: exception-runbook-draft.md (markdown, 6 KB)

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 08:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated per-route economics view + exception runbook

Looks good. Quick notes from a UX/implementation angle:
- Card vs table: build a compact card for each route, but allow an expandable table view for bulk operations (export, tag, open incident).
- Sampling: for high-volume tenants we should sample tokens for latency percentiles with reservoir sampling. Full p99 for all routes will be expensive.
- Cost attribution: route -> model variant -> tenant mapping must be present so per-route cost is actionable. Recommend a mapping import CSV (example format in your attachment).
- OSS components: we can reuse the console sparkline and heatmap widgets; estimate a week for the dashboard front-end and 3 days for backend aggregation endpoints if Markus can add the metric labels this week.

I will create the wireframe mock and push to the shared drive link. Putting a TODO for service owners to confirm route-to-tenant mapping.

Ava
Product Designer, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Walsh <emma@nimbushealth.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated per-route economics view + exception runbook

Emma, Dylan, team — thanks for the context and draft. Short update and next steps: 

Summary for Emma: we will deliver a console wireframe and a first-run exception runbook next week. The runbook will include detection thresholds, immediate mitigation steps (rate limits, fallback to cheaper model variants, temporary traffic caps), and who to loop in for postmortem.

Action items assigned:
- Markus: add route and variant labels to our metrics and add aggregation endpoints (ETA: 3 business days)
- Ava: wireframe mock for per-route cards and expandable table (ETA: 5 business days)
- Dylan: finalize runbook draft and turn into a markdown doc we can share (ETA: 3 business days)
- Emma/ops: confirm route-to-tenant mapping and share any internal budget thresholds we should encode into alerts (ETA: EOD Friday)

Proposed sync: 30-minute alignment on Thu 19 Aug at 10:30am PT. Will send calendar invite once Emma confirms.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
